assumptions.choice: Implemented 'Moving Average (Linear Regression)' as a manual least-squares regression endpoint (LSMA) computed each bar over the trailing 120 closes, via a small nested indicator class.
assumptions.reason: Backtrader's pure-python indicator set has no bundled plain LinearRegression class outside the optional statsmodels-based OLS indicators (statsmodels is not in the allowed import list), so a dependency-free manual computation is the literal, portable reading of 'Moving Average - Linear Regression.'

assumptions.choice: Used the bar's Close price as 'price' throughout (Z-score numerator, MA input, StdDev input).
assumptions.reason: The spec does not specify which OHLC field; Close is the conventional default for this kind of indicator input.

assumptions.choice: Standard deviation computed via backtrader's built-in StandardDeviation indicator (SMA-based rolling population standard deviation of Close) over the same 120-bar period.
assumptions.reason: Literal, standard reading of 'Standard Deviation, period 120 hours' as an independent rolling statistic, not tied to the linear-regression residuals.

assumptions.choice: Entry conditions (Z>0 long / Z<0 short) are evaluated as plain threshold checks each bar while flat, not strict cross-over events.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'becomes greater than 0' without defining a cross detector; combined with the 'one position at a time' default, a level check while flat reproduces 'opens when Z first becomes positive/negative after being flat.'

assumptions.choice: Implemented both the fixed 5% stop-loss and the 1% trailing stop as native backtrader Stop / StopTrail broker orders, submitted immediately after entry fill and linked One-Cancels-Other so whichever triggers first closes the position and cancels the other; a Z-score exit also cancels both pending protective orders before issuing the close.
assumptions.reason: This is the standard, idiomatic backtrader mechanism for reproducing 'fixed % stop from entry' and 'trailing % from the running high/low' exactly, and running both concurrently matches the spec's literal wording that both risk controls apply to every trade.

assumptions.choice: Sized each new entry as (available portfolio value x 99%) / current close price, with fractional units allowed.
assumptions.reason: Spec states '100% of capital on each trade'; a 1% buffer is reserved because the order fills on the following bar's open (price may have moved) and a 0.1% commission must still be covered, avoiding spurious margin rejections that a literal 100% could trigger.

assumptions.choice: Short entries/exits and short-side stop-loss/trailing-stop mirror the long-side rules (buy-stop above entry, trailing off the running low).
assumptions.reason: The spec explicitly extends both the entry/exit rules and the stop-loss/trailing-stop rules to shorts ('or the minimum for a short'), so symmetry is the literal reading, not an invented addition.
